purpose: E168 showed that subwin_mean (N non-overlapping sub-windows, each run through the full E65 pipeline, then averaged over the 855-d features) is a genuinely new information source: N=4 diagnostic AUC 0.7822 vs E65 0.7578, and the AUC rose monotonically with N (2/3/4). This run extends the sub-window count to N=1/2/3/4/6/8/12, tests multi-scale concatenation (N=2/3/4/6 blocks), fuses the amplitude stream (logbp) with the sub-window stream at feature level and score level, and finally runs the E159/E169-style frozen-score ceiling analysis on the best configuration to ask whether the new ranking power pushes the W upper bound past 0.80.

logbp.note: 90-d log band power, channel-major column order (channel*5 + band), E146 cache

E169_ceiling_E65_logbp.note: E169 table 1 / table 2 for the same E65+logbp control

E168_subwin_mean.note: E168 best diagnostic AUC per N (PCA-64 k=12)

subwindow.rules: trial 18x1200 is cut along time into N non-overlapping windows (length 1200/N); every window independently runs the full E65 pipeline (5-band ideal FFT band isolation -> mean removal -> per-channel standardisation -> 18x18 correlation -> 0.05 shrinkage -> logSPD -> upper triangle 171 -> E36 detrend_zband). The N window vectors (855 each) are averaged; no cross-sample statistic is introduced.
subwindow.note: N=1 must reproduce the E65 cache bit-for-bit and the E143 protocol numbers exactly; the sub-window mean is NOT equivalent to the full trial because detrend_zband is non-linear.

evaluation.protocol: E143/E168 verbatim: task-wise z-score using all Train rows of that task -> PCA fitted on fit_rows (frac<=0.6) -> k-means prototypes -> 5-block Train OOF thresholds (acceptance grid 0.80-0.96) -> LOSO excluding the scored identity with fit_rows-only prototypes and evaluation block 0.6<frac<=0.8 -> Test scored once, session used only for the diagnostic AUC
evaluation.train_oof_definition: Train OOF known-vs-LOSO-unknown AUROC; OOF F1 is the 20-class macro F1 of the 5-block OOF identity predictions

score_fusion.note: z-score every stream with its own 5-block Train OOF mean/std, then take a convex combination. The full 0.1 simplex is reported as a Test-selected sweep; the defensible number is the weight vector chosen by the fused Train LOSO AUC (Test never consulted).

ceiling_analysis.method: E159/E169: freeze one configuration's Train-OOF and Test scores, sweep a single frozen threshold over 2000 quantiles of the pooled distribution, and record acceptance / LOSO rejection / S1 rejection / S2 acceptance / W at every point.
ceiling_analysis.oracle_max_W: maximum W along the sweep with the LOSO rejection taken at the same threshold (optimistic: LOSO -> 1 as acceptance -> 0)
ceiling_analysis.E159_convention: LOSO fixed at the configuration's own @0.90 value, Test operating point free; this is the convention that produced 0.7704 for E65+logbp in E169
ceiling_analysis.loose_convention: LOSO fixed at the configuration's maximum over the protocol acceptance grid 0.80-0.96, Test operating point free (strictest optimistic bound)

targets.note: E169 slope: +0.042 diagnostic AUC buys +0.035 W upper bound, so AUC ~0.835 is needed for the upper bound to cross 0.80
